  • Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Proficiency in Go or Python, with strong production-grade system design capabilities and the ability to produce high-quality Technical Requirements Documents (TRDs).
  1. LLM Application Engineering
  • Strong expertise in LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and the ReAct pattern.
  • Experience in context window management, including token budgeting, conversation history compression, and sub-agent context compression.
  1. Production-Grade Agent Experience
  • Proven experience taking an Agent system from zero to production and establishing a continuous improvement lifecycle.

  1. Hands-on Agent Engineering
  • Familiarity with at least one Agent orchestration framework, such as LangGraph, Dify, Eino, Embabel, or OpenAI Agents SDK.
  • Practical experience with multi-agent collaboration, including Agent Teams, parallel execution, DAG-based orchestration, or handoffs.
  1. Complementary Agent Capabilities — Deep Expertise in at Least One Area
  • RAG engineering: vector retrieval, hybrid search, and reranking.
  • Evaluation frameworks: LLM-as-a-Judge, Golden Sets, regression testing, and A/B testing.
  1. Engineering Discipline
  • Ability to quantify Agent effectiveness and cost, with a strong focus on token efficiency.
  • Understanding of PII masking and prompt injection prevention.
  • Ability to identify regulatory and compliance boundaries in financial applications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Zero-to-one experience building Agent simulation or benchmarking platforms comparable in scope to τ-Bench.
  • Experience with self-hosted LLM deployment, including inference frameworks such as vLLM and Triton, and models such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and GLM.
  • Domain-specific AI application experience: Crypto and financial AI (risk management, KYC, compliance), AIOps (alert RCA and build diagnostics), customer service AI, or AI-powered software engineering.
  • Publicly demonstrated AI security research, including prompt injection prevention, jailbreak mitigation, or AI-powered smart contract security.
  • Core contributions to open-source projects such as LangChain, LangGraph, Dify, MCP, Eino, or Vercel AI SDK.

Translate a researcher's model and a trader's instinct into production strategy code that holds up when markets don't.

Overview

As an Algo Developer, you'll take trading strategies that our researchers and traders have validated and build them into production code. You'll own each change from specification to release, then stay with it once it's live, measuring how it behaves and fixing what breaks. The work sits where research meets engineering, and small implementation details show up in profit and loss (P&L).

What you'll be doing

Strategy implementation

  • Build new strategies and changes to existing ones from research specifications, working alongside the researcher who wrote them
  • Question a specification when the data or the code suggests it won't behave as intended

Testing and release

  • Write tests and run simulations that show a change does what it should before it trades
  • Take changes through code review and staged rollouts, and own each release from merge to live

Performance

  • Profile strategy code and cut latency and memory overhead on the paths that matter
  • Compare live behavior against the backtest and track down the gaps

Production support

  • Investigate incidents traced to strategy code, from a misplaced order to an unexpected position
  • Improve the tools, logs and monitoring the team uses to find problems faster

The ideal candidate

Engineering

  • Experience shipping performance-sensitive code to production in a compiled language such as C#, C++, Rust or Java
  • A working grasp of concurrency, memory allocation and latency measurement, and the habit of testing what you build

Markets

  • Exposure to trading systems, market data or exchange connectivity, in crypto or traditional markets
  • Curiosity about how market-making and systematic strategies make and lose money, and comfort turning the maths in a research specification into code

How you work

  • Ownership of what you ship, including after it goes live
  • Clear, short communication with traders and researchers when time is tight
  • Judgment about when to move fast and when to stop and check

You'll own our internal financial reporting engine and reconciliation platform, and make sure every product we build, including the products we're building with Mastercard, goes live with the right reconciliation and reporting in place.

You'll work closely with the Reconciliation Operations and Operations Delivery teams to understand where breaks and manual work come from, and turn that into a prioritised backlog. You'll also partner with finance, treasury and compliance, who rely on accurate reconciliation for safeguarding, month-end close and regulatory reporting.

You'll work with engineers across the payments, wallets and ledger teams on the data structures and events that reconciliation depends on, and with small, autonomous engineering squads across BVNK. We see AI as a key lever in how we build, and we expect you to use it in your day-to-day work.

Agents are starting to move money on people's behalf, and every transaction has to be fast, correct and auditable the first time. The infrastructure that makes this safe is being built now, and the team building it needs an engineering manager who ships quickly without breaking the money.

You'll manage a team of Sapiom engineers and grow it over the next year, partnering with our product manager to turn the roadmap into shipped product. The right person has managed payments or fintech engineers, still ships real code, and treats reliable, on-time delivery as a craft. Own execution for your team end to end: how it plans, builds, ships and runs its part of Sapiom's stack, from APIs and SDKs to the ledger and infrastructure behind every transaction.
